intro.title: The system: deca-alanine
facts: System. Ace-(Ala)10-Nme: ten alanines with capped ends, 112 atoms, in vacuum. AMBER ff14SB, 300 K, Langevin dynamics, 2 fs steps. Simulated with OpenMM 8.6.1 (CPU platform), openmmtools 0.26.0 and pymbar 4.2.0.

Why vacuum. With no water the system is tiny, so it is very fast to simulate (≈ 830 ns/day per CPU core), which makes it a good demo of enhanced sampling. But its specific behavior differs from the solvated peptide: water competes for the backbone H-bonds, so in solution the helix is far less stable and the free-energy profile much flatter.

The coordinate. dee is the distance from the ACE carbonyl carbon to the NME nitrogen, so it spans all ten residues. An α-helix rises 1.5 Å per residue (dee ≈ 15 Å); a fully stretched chain gives ≈ 3.4 Å per residue (≈ 33 Å).
A classic benchmark. Park, Khalili-Araghi, Tajkhorshid & Schulten (J. Chem. Phys. 2003) used this exact helix→coil stretch in vacuum to test free energies from steered MD and Jarzynski's equality.

Why the helix is so stable here. In vacuum no water competes for the backbone's i→i+4 H-bonds (up to 8 here), so pulling the helix apart means breaking them one by one. Our reference puts F(30 Å) − F(15 Å) at ≈ 23 kcal/mol.

A third state. In this vacuum model the chain can also fold back on itself into compact states (dee < 8 Å) with roughly the helix's free energy. This is a prediction of the model, not an established structure.

What makes it a good test. dee is an intuitive slow coordinate, but it hides a second barrier (breaking H-bonds) that it cannot see directly. Methods that bias or bin on dee alone feel that hidden barrier; methods that need no coordinate do not, but pay in other ways.
intro.welcome: Welcome! This tool lets you explore different enhanced sampling algorithms on a small but interesting test system, deca-alanine in vacuum. Developed by Daniel D. Richman, Dror Lab, Stanford, 2026.

estimators.title: Estimators on the umbrella-sampling data
estimators.blurb: Same 42 umbrella windows, five ways to turn them into a free-energy profile. MBAR weights every sample optimally and needs no bins; WHAM is its binned approximation (shown at 0.5 Å and 2 Å bins, to expose the binning error MBAR avoids); umbrella integration uses only each window's mean and variance; stitching unbiases each window's histogram separately and glues neighbours by their overlap.
estimators.fe_how: all estimators see exactly the same samples (every 2 ps); error is measured against full-data MBAR

system.name: Ace-(Ala)10-Nme, vacuum, ff14SB, 300 K
system.blurb: Ten enhanced-sampling methods on one small peptide. Deca-alanine in vacuum: a stable α-helix (d_ee ≈ 15 Å) that can unravel to an extended chain (≈ 33 Å) or fold over into compact states. Plain MD stays near the helix.

methods.name: Plain MD
methods.blurb: Unbiased Langevin dynamics at 300 K for 20 ns. The baseline: it samples the helix and the compact states but never reaches the extended chain, so it says nothing about the uphill side of the profile.
methods.fe_how: F(d_ee) = −kT ln P(d_ee), from the trajectory histogram.

methods.name: Well-tempered metadynamics
methods.blurb: Every 1 ps a Gaussian (1.2 kJ/mol high, 0.5 Å wide) is added to a bias on d_ee at the walker's position, pushing it away from where it has already been. Well-tempered: heights shrink as exp(−V/kΔT) with γ = 10, so the bias converges instead of overfilling.
methods.fe_how: F(s) = −γ/(γ−1) · V(s) + const, read directly from the bias.

methods.name: Gaussian accelerated MD
methods.blurb: Dual-boost Gaussian accelerated MD: whenever the total or dihedral energy V is below a threshold E, a harmonic boost ½k(E−V)² is added, lifting every energy basin without choosing a CV. E and k come from a short conventional run and keep the boost near-Gaussian (σ₀ = 6 kcal/mol).
methods.fe_how: Frames reweighted by exp(βΔV); per bin via a 2nd-order cumulant expansion.

methods.name: Temperature REMD
methods.blurb: Temperature replica exchange: 10 copies at 300–700 K run side by side, and every 1 ps neighbouring temperatures attempt a Metropolis swap. Hot copies cross barriers and hand their configurations down to 300 K. No CV.
methods.fe_how: MBAR over all replicas and temperatures, evaluated at 300 K.

methods.name: SAMS over temperature (simulated tempering)
methods.blurb: Self-adjusting mixture sampling over temperature (simulated tempering): one copy hops among 12 temperatures (300–700 K) while SAMS learns each temperature's free energy on the fly, so all are visited equally. No CV.
methods.fe_how: MBAR over the walker's samples at all temperatures, evaluated at 300 K.

methods.name: SAMS (adaptive umbrellas)
methods.blurb: Self-adjusting mixture sampling over umbrellas: one copy hops among 42 harmonic restraints on d_ee (4–35 Å) while SAMS learns each restraint's free energy on the fly, so all are visited equally. Adaptive umbrella sampling with a single walker.
methods.fe_how: MBAR over all umbrella states; SAMS's online log Z is a smoothed estimate of the same profile.

methods.name: Weighted ensemble (bins on d_ee)
methods.blurb: Weighted ensemble: many short (10 ps) unbiased walkers, each carrying a probability weight. After each segment, walkers are split in under-occupied 1 Å d_ee bins and merged in over-occupied ones (4 per bin), conserving total weight exactly. It stalls near 21 Å, where going further means breaking helical H-bonds that d_ee bins cannot see.
methods.fe_how: F(bin) = −kT ln(total walker weight in the bin).

methods.name: Weighted ensemble (bins on d_ee × H-bonds)
methods.blurb: The same weighted ensemble, binned on (d_ee, number of helical H-bonds), so walkers that start to lose H-bonds get their own bins and are split. More bins means more walkers per iteration, and so fewer iterations for the same cost.
methods.fe_how: F(bin) = −kT ln(total walker weight), summed over H-bond bins onto d_ee.

methods.name: Steered MD + Jarzynski
methods.blurb: Steered MD: a spring (7.2 kcal/mol/Å²) drags d_ee from the helix to 34 Å at constant speed, far from equilibrium; 32 pulls at 10 Å/ns and 32 at 100 Å/ns. Jarzynski's equality recovers the equilibrium free energy from the work distribution.

methods.name: Umbrella sampling + MBAR (reference)
methods.blurb: Umbrella sampling: 42 independent windows, each restrained near a fixed d_ee (4–35 Å, 2 kcal/mol/Å²) for 3 ns, seeded from one fast pull. Windows never exchange; MBAR combines them afterwards. This is the reference curve on every page.
